t: Number of Prefix Connected Groups — Count Prefix Buckets
o: Two words are connected iff their first k characters match; connectivity is an equivalence relation, so groups are just buckets of equal k-prefixes. Words shorter than k are ignored, duplicates count separately. Example 3: prefix 'bat' appears twice and 'dog' three times → 2 groups. We only need to count buckets whose size ≥ 2.
k: Truncate each word of length ≥ k to its first k characters.
Count occurrences per prefix with a hash map.
Answer = number of prefixes occurring at least twice.

a.i: One pass building a frequency map of k-prefixes, then count entries with frequency ≥ 2.
s: Iterate words; skip those shorter than k.
Sum the number of keys with count ≥ 2.
a.t: O(total characters) — hashing each truncated prefix once

a.i: Sorting the truncated prefixes puts equal prefixes adjacent; scan runs and count runs of length ≥ 2.
s: Collect word[:k] for eligible words into a list and sort it.
Add 1 for each run of length ≥ 2.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def countPrefixConnectedGroups(self, words, k):
        ws = sorted(w[:k] for w in words if len(w) >= k)
        ans = 0
        i = 0
        while i < len(ws):
            j = i
            while j < len(ws) and ws[j] == ws[i]: j += 1
            if j - i >= 2: ans += 1
            i = j
        return ans

a.t: O(G log G · k) — sorting G prefixes of length k

w: Prefer the hash-map version for its linear time; the sort version avoids hashing overhead and is easier to adapt to streaming input. Pitfalls: forgetting the length < k filter, and remembering duplicates count toward group size (Example 3). Follow-up: report the group sizes, or handle k larger than some words dynamically.
